title: DoppelVet: Comparative Safety Verification for Self-Evolving Agents
abstract: arXiv:2611.29306v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Self-evolving agents improve by retaining feedback as reusable memories or skills, but every mistaken approval can shape many future behaviors. Two updates can provide exactly the same evidence to a verifier yet produce opposite safety outcomes, so the verifier cannot distinguish them from that evidence alone. We introduce DoppelVet, a verification framework that checks proposed updates before they enter an agent's persistent state. Without access to safety labels, DoppelVet constructs an alternative that matches every signal used by the existing verifier. It replays both updates from the same state and directly compares their behaviors in both presentation orders before deciding whether to retain the candidate. We evaluate DoppelVet on DoppelVet-Grid and DoppelVet-Tool, covering executable programs and natural-language memories. Across nine open-weight and proprietary verifiers, DoppelVet raises mean harmful-update detection AUC from 0.

translated_title: DoppelVet：面向自我进化智能体的对比式安全验证
translated_abstract: 自我进化智能体通过将反馈保存为可复用的记忆或技能来不断改进，但每一次错误的批准都可能影响其未来许多行为。两个更新可能向验证器提供完全相同的证据，却产生截然相反的安全结果，因此验证器仅凭这些证据无法区分它们。我们提出了 DoppelVet，这是一个在提议更新进入智能体持久状态之前对其进行审查的验证框架。在无法获取安全标签的情况下，DoppelVet 会构造一个与现有验证器所使用的所有信号完全匹配的替代更新。它从同一状态回放这两个更新，并在两种呈现顺序下直接比较它们的行为，然后再决定是否保留候选更新。我们在 DoppelVet-Grid 和 DoppelVet-Tool 两个基准上评估了 DoppelVet，涵盖可执行程序和自然语言记忆两类场景。在九个开源权重及专有验证器上，DoppelVet 将平均有害更新检测 AUC 从 0……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: DoppelVet 提出了一种对比式安全验证框架：在不依赖安全标签的情况下，构造一个与候选更新向验证器提供的所有信号完全匹配的替代更新，通过从同一状态在两种顺序下回放并直接比较两者行为，来识别仅凭证据本身无法区分的有害更新。
en_tdlr: DoppelVet is a comparative safety verification framework that, without safety labels, constructs an alternative update matching every signal the verifier receives, replays both updates from the same state in both presentation orders, and directly compares their behaviors to catch harmful updates that are indistinguishable from evidence alone.
